subtitle: When a Scholar-King Fell, Two Lions Moved

panels.shot: epic wide shot from above the Malwa plateau
panels.action: Bhima I of Anhilwara sits astride a war elephant atop a rocky ridge overlooking the misty plains of Malwa, banners of Gujarat whipping in the wind as distant temple-towers and the city of Dhara lie small on the horizon.

dialogue.text: As Bhoja of Malwa, the poet-king, lay still, Bhima of Gujarat and Karna of Tripuri moved—was this glory, or the shadow at its edge?

i18n.hi: कवि‑राजा मालवा के भोज शांत पड़े थे, तब गुजरात के भीम और तृिपुरी के कर्ण चले—ये महिमा थी, या उसकी कगार की परछाईं?

panels.shot: slow pull-in over a map-table
panels.action: A parchment map of western and central India lies on a wooden table, etched with ranges and rivers; small carved elephants mark Anhilwara and Tripuri, a lion emblem rests over Dhara, and a single oil lamp throws long shadows.

dialogue.text: Mid-eleventh century. From the Sabarmati to the Narmada, kingdoms watched each other with tired eyes and sharpened spears.

i18n.hi: ग्यारहवीं सदी का मध्य। साबरमती से नर्मदा तक, राज्य थकी आँखों और तेज भालों से एक‑दूसरे को तौल रहे थे।

panels.shot: poetic wide shot of Dhara at dusk
panels.action: The hilltop city of Dhara spreads under a purple sky, crowned by a great palace and temple spires; scholars walk in courtyards, palm-leaf manuscripts in hand, while artisans raise a pillared hall.

dialogue.text: At Dhara, Bhoja of the Paramaras ruled—a king remembered not for raids, but for verses, debates and stone.

i18n.hi: धारा में परमार भोज राज कर रहे थे—छापों से नहीं, कविताओं, वाद‑विवादों और पत्थर से याद किए जाने वाले राजा।

panels.shot: intimate interior, low-angle on Bhoja's couch
panels.action: An aging Bhoja reclines on a low couch, thin but dignified, surrounded by worried courtiers and brahmana scholars; through a window, the faint outline of Dhara’s ramparts glows in sunset light.

dialogue.text: Later Jain prabandhas say: as Bhoja’s body failed, word of his fading reached courts far beyond the Vindhyas.

i18n.hi: बाद के जैन प्रबंध कहते हैं: जैसे‑जैसे भोज का शरीर टूट रहा था, उनके ढलने की खबर विन्ध्य से बहुत दूर दरबारों तक जा पहुँची।

panels.shot: medium shot in royal council chamber, slow push-in
panels.action: Bhima I stands in the pillared hall of Anhilwara, young but hardened, hand resting on his sword-hilt as ministers present dispatches; a painted map of Malwa adorns the wall behind him.

dialogue.text: In Anhilwara, Bhima I of the Chaulukyas heard that the scholar of Dhara might not see another monsoon.

i18n.hi: अणहिलवाड़ा में, चालुक्य भीम प्रथम ने सुना कि धारा का पंडित‑राजा शायद अगला मानसून न देख पाए।

panels.shot: close-up on Bhima's face, half in shadow
panels.action: Bhima’s face fills the frame, one side lit by the hall’s light, the other in shadow, his eyes narrowed in thought as he looks down at a report in his hand.

dialogue.speaker: Bhima I of Anhilwara
dialogue.text: When a lion grows weak, the forest changes.

i18n.hi: जब शेर ढीला पड़ता है, जंगल का रंग बदल जाता है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over Anhilwara’s ramparts and mustering troops
panels.action: From above the fortified city of Anhilwara, rows of Chaulukya soldiers assemble in the courtyard, elephants and cavalry lining up as Bhima watches from the ramparts, cloak snapping in the wind.

dialogue.text: Inscriptional hints and later tales agree: Gujarat’s gaze turned east, towards Bhoja’s Malwa.

i18n.hi: शिलालेखों के इशारे और बाद की कथाएँ मिलकर कहती हैं: गुजरात की निगाहें पूरब, भोज के मालवा पर टिक गईं।

panels.shot: transition shot, map dissolving into landscape march
panels.action: A stylised map showing Anhilwara and Tripuri linked by bold lines dissolves into a real landscape of marching columns crossing a dry riverbed, Chaulukya and Kalachuri banners fluttering side by side.

dialogue.text: Some epigraphs speak of a joint storm—Bhima of Gujarat and Karna of Tripuri, moving together against Malwa.

i18n.hi: कुछ लेख संयुक्त तूफ़ान की बात करते हैं—गुजरात के भीम और तृिपुरी के कर्ण, साथ‑साथ मालवा पर बढ़ते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot on plateau road, armies converging
panels.action: On a dusty plateau road lined with thorn scrub, two great armies converge from opposite horizons; Bhima rides at the head of his column, turning slightly as if to greet an unseen ally over the rise.

dialogue.text: For years, Paramaras, Chaulukyas and Kalachuris had wrestled over this plateau. Now, two rivals chose to share the prize.

i18n.hi: बरसों से परमार, चालुक्य और कलचुरि इस पठार पर भिड़ते रहे थे। अब दो विरोधी ने तय किया कि इनाम बाँट लिया जाए।

panels.shot: somber interior of a Jain monastery library
panels.action: Inside a quiet Jain monastery, the monk Merutunga, imagined centuries later, sits cross-legged amid shelves of palm-leaf manuscripts, his stylus poised as he listens to an elder recite tales of Bhoja and Bhima.

dialogue.text: Centuries on, Merutunga would write in his Prabandhachintamani of how they fell on Dhara as Bhoja lay dying.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद मेरुतुंग ने अपने ‘प्रबंधचिंतामणि’ में लिखा कि कैसे वे धारा पर टूट पड़े, जब भोज मृत्युशय्या पर थे।

panels.shot: close-up of palm-leaf manuscript being inscribed
panels.action: A hand carefully scratches letters onto a palm-leaf, the script forming the famous lament verse, while a small lamp flickers beside it, casting trembling shadows across the text.

dialogue.text: He preserved a lament: that when Bhoja died, Sarasvati herself wept. Memory itself seemed uneasy at the timing of the attack.

i18n.hi: वह एक विलाप सँजोता है: कि भोज की मृत्यु पर स्वयं सरस्वती रो पड़ीं। याद ही को इस हमले की घड़ी पर बेचैनी थी।

panels.shot: low-angle on Dhara’s walls with approaching dust cloud
panels.action: From below Dhara’s stone walls, the camera shows a distant rising dust cloud on the plain; silhouettes of elephants and cavalry can just be seen, while townsfolk and guards stand tense on the battlements.

dialogue.text: Exact dates and movements blur in the sources, but all agree: Malwa was struck while its great king was gone or going.

i18n.hi: तारीखें और कदम स्रोतों में धुँधला जाते हैं, पर सब मानते हैं: मालवा पर चोट तब पड़ी, जब उसका महान राजा जा चुका था, या जाता हुआ था।

panels.shot: dramatic medium-wide outside Dhara’s gate
panels.action: Bhima, armored and resolute, sits on his elephant before Dhara’s closed gates; behind him, rows of Chaulukya troops wait, while siege engines are dragged forward under the gaze of cloudy skies.

dialogue.text: To Bhima, this was the hour to avenge old slights, to push Chaulukya spears beyond the Narmada.

i18n.hi: भीम के लिए यही घड़ी थी पुराने अपमान चुकाने की, चालुक्य के भालों को नर्मदा के पार धकेलने की।

panels.shot: wide battle tableau at a remove, no gore
panels.action: On an open field near Dhara, opposing lines clash from a distant vantage: shields raised, horses rearing, dust swirling, while the city’s towers watch in the background, untouched by detail.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions remember victories; they do not show the burned homes, the broken walls, the families on the road.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख जीतों को रखते हैं; जली बस्तियाँ, गिरे परकोटे, रास्तों पर भटकते परिवार वे नहीं दिखाते।

panels.shot: somber interior of a small shrine in Malwa
panels.action: Inside a village shrine, an elderly woman removes garlands from a soot-darkened image while a child clings to her; through the doorway, soldiers march past with plundered goods on carts.

dialogue.text: Yet the Jain chronicler hints at temples shaken, scholars scattered, and a court of learning suddenly gone silent.

i18n.hi: फिर भी जैन इतिहासकार इशारा करता है हिलते मंदिरों की, बिखरते पंडितों की, और अचानक मौन हो चली विद्या‑सभा की।

panels.shot: map-table again, now with tokens rearranged
panels.action: The same wooden map-table returns; this time the lion emblem over Dhara has been split, one half moved toward the Chaulukya elephant marker, the other toward the Kalachuri symbol, as a hand divides them with a straightedge.

dialogue.text: Tradition says Malwa was partitioned—Bhima took the west, Karna the east. But the lines were drawn on parchment, not yet in men’s minds.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कहती है मालवा बाँट दिया गया—पश्चिम भीम के हिस्से, पूरब कर्ण के। पर ये लकीरें अभी सिर्फ कागज़ पर थीं, लोगों के मन में नहीं।

panels.shot: interior of Bhima’s court, trophies displayed
panels.action: Back in the ornate hall of Anhilwara, Bhima sits on his lion throne as courtiers present a captured parasol and a jeweled manuscript; musicians play softly while a few ministers exchange uneasy glances.

dialogue.text: In Gujarat, poets praised Bhima as conqueror of Malwa. Epigraphs spoke proudly of his reach beyond his own plain.

i18n.hi: गुजरात में कवि भीम की मालवा‑विजय गाते रहे। शिलालेखों ने गर्व से उसके अपने मैदान से परे तक बढ़े हाथ का बखान किया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Dhara slowly stirring back to life
panels.action: Dhara’s streets, once scarred and quiet, now show signs of recovery: new scaffolding on temples, merchants reopening shops, a new Paramara prince riding through the gate with a small escort.

dialogue.text: But the Paramaras did not vanish. Under Bhoja’s successors, Malwa rose again, its prashastis reclaiming honor and space.

i18n.hi: पर परमार मिटे नहीं। भोज के उत्तराधिकारियों के नीचे मालवा फिर उठा, उसकी प्रशस्तियाँ फिर मान‑सम्मान और जगह माँगने लगीं।

panels.shot: forward-looking shot, young Siddharaja in training yard (foreshadow)
panels.action: In a training yard at Anhilwara, a young prince Siddharaja practices with wooden sword and shield under a tutor’s eye, while in the background a wall-painting shows Bhima’s campaign in faint colors.

dialogue.text: These unfinished borders would later draw Bhima’s heir, Siddharaja, into fresh wars with Malwa’s kings.

i18n.hi: इन अधूरे सरहदों ने आगे चलकर भीम के उत्तराधिकारी सिद्धराज को फिर नए युद्धों में खींचा, मालवा के राजाओं के साथ।

panels.shot: introspective close-up of older Bhima at dusk
panels.action: An older Bhima stands alone on a terrace at dusk, looking eastward; the wind tugs at his cloak, and below, the torches of Anhilwara flicker like scattered stars.

dialogue.text: Bhima’s name endures in stone and verse—as the king who fled one invader, and later struck a neighbor in his last hour.

i18n.hi: भीम का नाम पत्थर और कविता दोनों में दर्ज है—एक ऐसा राजा, जो एक आक्रमणकारी से भागा, पर बाद में पड़ोसी पर उसकी आखिरी घड़ी में टूट पड़ा।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide over the Malwa-Gujarat landscape
panels.action: A dawn panorama stretches from the rivers and plains of Malwa to the fields of Gujarat, bathed in soft light; distant cities glimmer faintly, while birds rise from the forests between.

dialogue.text: Honest memory holds both the courage and the timing of Bhima’s march on Malwa, and asks us to see power not only in what it wins, but in how it chooses to win.

i18n.hi: ईमानदार स्मृति भीम की मालवा‑चढ़ाई में साहस भी देखती है और उसकी घड़ी भी, और हमसे कहती है ताकत को सिर्फ जीत से नहीं, जीतने के तरीके से भी तौलो।

title_i18n.en: Bhima I and the Fall of Bhoja's Malwa
title_i18n.hi: भीम प्रथम और भोज का ढहता मालवा

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Scholar-King Fell, Two Lions Moved
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक विद्वान राजा गिरा, तो दो शेर चले
